title: Compaction triggers + per-interval budget (guardrails to avoid thrash)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Implement online compaction trigger policy + a hard budget model so compaction reduces fragmentation/tail latency without introducing median latency regressions or compaction/eviction thrash.

Context
Under bursty traffic + mixed sequence lengths, allocator fragmentation increases allocation overhead and drives p95/p99 spikes. We need a deterministic trigger + budget that:
- Runs when it helps (fragmentation/pressure)
- Stops when it hurts (over-budget / no progress)
- Avoids repeated compact/allocate/compact loops

Scope
1) Threshold-based triggers
- Trigger compaction when fragmentation ratio exceeds threshold AND there is allocation pressure OR we are nearing soft cap.
- Trigger compaction on allocation failure as a last resort (bounded attempt, then fall back to eviction/backpressure).
- Add minimum “cooldown” between compaction passes per device/pool to avoid oscillation.

2) Per-interval compaction budget
- Budget compaction work in a rolling interval (e.g., per 100ms or per scheduling tick).
- Enforce maximum bytes moved and maximum wall-clock time spent in compaction per interval.
- Budget is configurable via runtime flags; default is conservative.

3) Safety guardrails
- “No progress” detection: if a compaction pass moves <X blocks/bytes or does not improve fragmentation by >=Y points, stop and enter cooldown.
- Protect decode latency: do not start compaction if scheduler marks pool as latency-sensitive (e.g., high queueing delay / elevated p95) unless in allocation-failure path.
- Single compaction worker per device, with explicit mutual exclusion against other maintenance (eviction sweep) to avoid contention.
- Hard stop if compaction attempts exceed N per minute (thrash breaker) -> emit metric + structured log.

Non-goals
- Redesigning eviction policy (handled in ENG-2845)
- Implementing pointer move mechanics (handled in ENG-2844 + PR series)

Proposed trigger policy (v1)
Terminology (from metrics work in ENG-2842):
- fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_run_bytes / total_free_bytes) (or equivalent definition per allocator)
- alloc_pressure = allocator failure count or “near capacity” indicator

Trigger conditions:
A) Proactive compaction:
- if fragmentation_ratio >= FRAG_HIGH (default 0.35)
  AND total_free_bytes >= FREE_MIN_BYTES (avoid compacting when truly full)
  AND (alloc_pressure == true OR free_bytes < FREE_SOFT_CAP)
  AND last_compaction_end > COOLDOWN_MS

B) Allocation-failure fallback:
- On alloc failure: attempt one bounded compaction pass (budget multiplied by FAIL_MULT, default 2x)
- If still failing -> return pressure signal to scheduler (backpressure / eviction / route elsewhere).

Budget model (v1)
- budget_ms_per_interval (default 0.25ms)
- budget_bytes_per_interval (default 64MB)
- interval_ms (default 50ms)
- cap_moves_per_interval (default 512 blocks)

Stop conditions:
- stop when any budget exceeded
- stop when no-progress criteria met
- stop when allocator reports “low fragmentation” (fragmentation_ratio <= FRAG_TARGET, default 0.20)

Deliverables
- Runtime implementation behind compaction flag (plumbed by ENG-2848)
- Metrics for: trigger reason, budget used, bytes moved, number of passes, thrash breaker activations
- Unit tests for policy logic (cooldown/no-progress/budget enforcement)
- Perf regression sanity: compaction does not increase median latency > 1% in steady-state perf suite scenario

Acceptance criteria
- In bursty-mix benchmark: p99 improves vs baseline OR stays flat with measurable reduction in alloc failures; no statistically significant regression to p50.
- Compaction runs at most once per cooldown window when fragmentation is stable.
- Under allocation-failure scenario: at most 1 bounded attempt per failure event; emits a clear reason code.

Implementation notes
- Keep policy decision side-effect-free: compute ‘should_compact’ and ‘allowed_budget’ first, then execute.
- Ensure trigger evaluation is cheap; do not compute expensive fragmentation stats on every request. Use cached stats updated on allocator events.

comments: 2025-02-20 (Samir Qureshi): Drafted trigger policy proposal (FRAG_HIGH/FRAG_TARGET + cooldown + allocation-failure bounded attempt). Waiting on final fragmentation metric definition from ENG-2842 so thresholds map cleanly to dashboards.

2025-02-24 (Sofia Ivanova): Please ensure we can gate compaction when scheduler is in "latency sensitive" mode. We can expose a boolean from scheduler (queueing_delay_high) and treat it as an additional guardrail except for alloc-failure path.
2025-02-26 (Hiro Tanaka): Budget should be expressed in bytes moved + a small time cap; time cap alone is noisy due to stream sync effects. Suggest bytes cap primary, time cap secondary.

2025-03-01 (Allison Grant): For canary, need explicit trigger reason codes in metrics/logs (proactive_vs_alloc_failure_vs_thrash_breaker) so alerts can differentiate "healthy compaction" from "compaction thrashing".

2025-03-04 (Samir Qureshi): Implementation up in draft PR (internal branch) using rolling 50ms interval budget. Added thrash breaker: max 6 compaction starts / 60s / device. Added no-progress exit if frag improvement < 0.02 after pass. Requesting review from Omar + Sofia on guardrails and scheduler hook shape.
